title: Proteins and Amino Acids
content:
# Proteins and Amino Acids

## Learning Objectives
By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
- Describe the general structure of amino acids
- Explain how amino acids join to form polypeptides
- Describe the formation of peptide bonds
- Understand the diversity of proteins

## Introduction

**Proteins** are the most diverse biological molecules, performing thousands of different functions. All proteins are made from just 20 different **amino acids**. The sequence of amino acids determines the protein's shape and function.

## Key Concepts

### Elements in Proteins

**All proteins contain:**
- Carbon (C)
- Hydrogen (H)
- Oxygen (O)
- Nitrogen (N)

**Some proteins also contain:**
- Sulfur (S) - in some amino acids
- Other elements in prosthetic groups (e.g., Fe in haemoglobin)

### Amino Acid Structure

**All amino acids have:**
- Central carbon atom (α-carbon)
- Amino group (-NH₂)
- Carboxyl group (-COOH)
- Hydrogen atom (-H)
- R group (variable side chain)

[DIAGRAM: General amino acid structure]

**General formula:**
```
        H
        |
   H₂N-C-COOH
        |
        R
```

### The R Group

**What makes amino acids different:**
- R group is the variable part
- 20 different R groups = 20 amino acids
- R groups vary in size, charge, polarity
- Determines amino acid properties

| R group type | Properties | Examples |
|--------------|------------|----------|
| Non-polar | Hydrophobic | Glycine, alanine, valine |
| Polar | Hydrophilic | Serine, threonine |
| Acidic | Negative charge | Aspartic acid, glutamic acid |
| Basic | Positive charge | Lysine, arginine |
| Sulfur-containing | Can form disulfide bonds | Cysteine, methionine |

### The 20 Amino Acids

**Essential amino acids:**
- Cannot be made by the body
- Must come from diet
- 9 essential amino acids in humans

**Non-essential amino acids:**
- Can be synthesised by the body
- 11 non-essential amino acids

### Peptide Bond Formation

**Condensation reaction:**
- Amino group of one amino acid joins carboxyl group of another
- Water molecule released
- Peptide bond (C-N) forms

**Equation:**
$$\text{Amino acid} + \text{Amino acid} \rightarrow \text{Dipeptide} + H_2O$$

[DIAGRAM: Peptide bond formation between two amino acids]

### Polypeptides and Proteins

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| Dipeptide | 2 amino acids joined |
| Tripeptide | 3 amino acids joined |
| Polypeptide | Many amino acids joined (typically >20) |
| Protein | One or more polypeptides folded into functional shape |

**Sequence matters:**
- Order of amino acids = primary structure
- Different sequences = different proteins
- 20²⁰⁰ possible sequences for a 200 amino acid protein!

### Hydrolysis of Proteins

**Breaking peptide bonds:**
- Water added
- Peptide bonds broken
- Releases amino acids
- Catalysed by proteases/peptidases

**Occurs during:**
- Digestion (break down dietary proteins)
- Recycling of old proteins
- Protein turnover in cells

### Why So Many Proteins?

**Diversity comes from:**
- 20 different amino acids
- Variable chain lengths
- Different sequences possible
- Different 3D shapes

**Number of possible combinations:**
- For chain of n amino acids: 20ⁿ possibilities
- Even short chains have millions of possibilities

### Functions of Proteins

| Function | Example proteins |
|----------|------------------|
| Enzymes | Amylase, protease, lipase |
| Structure | Collagen, keratin |
| Transport | Haemoglobin, channel proteins |
| Defence | Antibodies |
| Hormones | Insulin, glucagon |
| Contraction | Actin, myosin |
| Storage | Casein (milk), albumin (egg) |
| Receptors | Hormone receptors |

### Importance of Amino Acid Sequence

**Sequence determines:**
- How the protein folds
- The 3D shape
- The function of the protein

**Example:** Sickle cell anaemia
- One amino acid change (glutamic acid → valine)
- Changes haemoglobin shape
- Causes serious disease

### Protein Diversity in Numbers

| Fact | Number |
|------|--------|
| Amino acid types | 20 |
| Proteins in human body | ~20,000 different types |
| Haemoglobin chain length | 574 amino acids (2 chains of 141 + 2 of 146) |
| Insulin length | 51 amino acids |
| Titin (largest) | ~27,000 amino acids |

## Common Exam Questions

- Draw the general structure of an amino acid
- Describe how a peptide bond is formed
- Explain what makes amino acids different from each other
- State the bond formed when amino acids join

## Common Misconceptions

- **Misconception:** All proteins are enzymes
- **Reality:** Enzymes are proteins, but proteins have many other functions

- **Misconception:** Amino acids and proteins are the same thing
- **Reality:** Amino acids are monomers; proteins are made of many amino acids

- **Misconception:** Only 20 proteins exist because there are 20 amino acids
- **Reality:** Thousands of different proteins exist through different sequences

- **Misconception:** Proteins only contain C, H, O, N
- **Reality:** Some proteins contain S, and prosthetic groups may contain other elements

## Practice Questions

1. Name the four elements found in all proteins. (2 marks)

2. Draw the general structure of an amino acid. (3 marks)

3. Describe how a peptide bond is formed. (3 marks)

4. Explain why there are thousands of different proteins when there are only 20 amino acids. (3 marks)

5. Define the terms dipeptide and polypeptide. (2 marks)

6. Discuss the importance of the sequence of amino acids in determining protein function. (6 marks)

## Key Terms Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| Amino acid | Monomer of proteins; has amino and carboxyl groups |
| R group | Variable side chain of amino acid |
| Peptide bond | Covalent bond between amino acids |
| Dipeptide | Two amino acids joined |
| Polypeptide | Chain of many amino acids |
| Protein | Functional molecule of one or more polypeptides |
| Essential amino acid | Must be obtained from diet |
| Condensation | Reaction joining amino acids, releasing water |

## Summary

- Proteins contain C, H, O, N (and sometimes S)
- Amino acids are the monomers of proteins
- All amino acids have: amino group, carboxyl group, H, and R group
- R group varies between the 20 amino acids
- Peptide bonds join amino acids (condensation reaction)
- Polypeptides are chains of amino acids; proteins are functional polypeptides
- Sequence of amino acids determines protein shape and function
- Proteins perform diverse functions: enzymes, structure, transport, defence, etc.
